$comment: Read 2026-09-29 from the handlers, not from the route name. The set is: every `endpoint` on a `method: 'GET'` entry in apps/web/src/lib/domains/page-catalog.ts, minus every endpoint already in CONTRACT_SHAPES in scripts/generate-resource-pages.mjs. That difference is 29 endpoints, not 50 — the table had already absorbed ~21 rows from two per-domain merges the same day (the two 'merged from the per-domain shape reports, 2026-09-29' blocks), several of which are duplicated verbatim across both blocks. Row count was verified against app.openapi(), which reports 552 paths. 25 of the 29 have a real GET; 4 do not and are under `defects`, not `shapes` — no shape was invented for them.
method: Paths were resolved with `app.openapi()` (552 paths), not `app.routes`. Four catalogue entries are 2026-09-29 readings of router prefixes, and two of the routers serving them (services/commerce/routers/commerce.py, services/validation/router.py) are not in services/api_gateway/routers/ at all.

Router prefix is /api/v1/commerce (main.py:608 includes it by alias `commerce_router`).

services/api_gateway/routers/tool_registry.py:217 `@router.get("/phases", response_model=list[int])` -> :221 `return sorted([row[0] for row in db.execute(stmt).all() if row[0]])`. app.openapi() confirms the 200 schema is `array<integer>`: a bare array, so `rowsKey` is null.

services/api_gateway/routers/ussd.py:103 `@router.get("/status")` -> :106 returns {"status": "requires_gateway", "note": "..."} — two keys, no array. The sibling `/api/v1/ussd/health` (ussd.py:74) does carry a list, but this is not that handler.

defects.evidence: services/api_gateway/routers/ai_chat.py:222 `@router.post("/chat", response_model=ChatResponse)` and services/api_gateway/routers/ai.py:68 `@router.post("/chat", response_model=QueryResponse)`; app.openapi() reports /api/v1/ai/chat with the method set ['post'] only. Neither provider serves a GET.
defects.fix: Expected, per the brief. No page should be generated. If the catalogue needs an AI read surface it is /api/v1/ai/history, which is already in CONTRACT_SHAPES as rows/conversations.

defects.evidence: services/api_gateway/routers/ecowallet.py:18 declares `router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/v1/ecowallet")` and registers no `""` route; main.py:522 mounts it with no extra prefix. app.openapi() publishes 11 `/api/v1/ecowallet/*` paths (daily-cap, earning-options, earnings, health, redemption-options, stats, wallet/{user_id}, and the POST earn/redeem/transfer/ussd/wallets) but not the bare prefix.
defects.fix: Either add a `@router.get("")` list-wallet handler, or repoint the catalogue entries at the two collection reads that already exist and carry the right shape: GET /api/v1/ecowallet/earnings and GET /api/v1/ecowallet/stats. A page pointed at /api/v1/ecowallet will 404 and render a permanent error state.

defects.evidence: services/api_gateway/routers/mrv.py:124 `@router.post("/lorawan-webhook")`; app.openapi() reports /api/v1/mrv/lorawan-webhook with ['post'] only. A LoRaWAN ingest webhook has no read side by design.
defects.fix: Catalogue `method` should be POST. No page.

defects.evidence: services/api_gateway/routers/newsletter.py:44 `@router.post("/subscribe")` -> :45 `def subscribe(payload: NewsletterSubscribe, ...)`; app.openapi() reports /api/v1/newsletter/subscribe with ['post'] only. The router declares no other route, so there is no subscriber list to read either.
defects.fix: Catalogue `method` should be POST. No page. If a subscriber list is wanted it has to be written first.

notes: No handler/response_model disagreement was found among the 25 read contracts, so unlike ManualCropsResponse there is no wire-vs-intent conflict to report here. The two places a model could have overridden the body — /api/v1/tool-registry (ToolListResponse) and /api/v1/hydroma/models (list[ModelMeta]) — were each checked against the body and agree.

The count is 29, not 50. CONTRACT_SHAPES had already grown by roughly 21 endpoints from two same-day 'merged from the per-domain shape reports' blocks before this work started, which is where the fifty went. Those two blocks also duplicate 8 rows verbatim between them (auth/sessions, manual/climate-normals/{site_id}, manual/sites/{site_id}, manual/weather-daily/{site_id}, marketplace/cart, marketplace/marketplaces, marketplace/orders, marketplace/payments), so the table reads as 168 rows but holds 160 distinct endpoints. Harmless to a lookup, but it should be collapsed before anyone counts the table as a list.

This file was derived against a 156-endpoint snapshot of CONTRACT_SHAPES. While it was being written the generator's owner merged 4 of the 25 rows independently: /api/v1/land/profiles, /api/v1/platform/stats and /api/v1/ussd/status, all of which agree with the readings here (rows / record / record), and /api/v1/models, which does not — see the fifth defect. The four are left in `shapes` so the coordinator can diff rather than reconcile; nothing else in the 29 changed.

Fifth defect, found in the peer's own merge rather than in a handler: the row just added as ['/api/v1/models', 'rows'] with no rowsKey is wrong, and its own comment proves why. It cites hydroma_dashboard.py:714 `@router.get("/models", response_model=list[ModelMeta])` returning `[ModelMeta(**m) for m in models]` at :734 — that is /api/v1/HYDROMA/models, a different route served by a different file. /api/v1/models is services/api_gateway/routers/models.py:14 `@router.get("", response_model=dict)`, whose handler models_index returns an envelope at :18: {"count": len(models), "fidelity_counts": {...}, "models": models}. A bare-array read of it gets undefined and renders a permanent empty state over 22 real models — the exact defect this table exists to prevent. It should be ['/api/v1/models', 'rows', 'models'].
